{
  "signals_observed": [
    "Alert date: 2025-05-17; merchant_id: 53; trigger_codes: [\"B\"].",
    "Trigger: AUP-06.1 breach: 30d chargeback rate 10.3% (3 disputes / 29 orders).",
    "cb_rate_30d: 0.10344827586206896; disputes_30d: 3; orders_30d: 29.",
    "gmv_30d: 1865874 cents; base_gmv: 3693188 cents; base_orders: 82; base_days: 90.",
    "volume_z: 0.31878835653166937; ticket_drift: 1.4285542967774443.",
    "new_gmv_30d: 266994 cents; new_gmv_share: 0.14309326353226423.",
    "refunds_30d: 0; refund_rate_30d: 0.0; base_refunds: 0; base_refund_rate: 0.0.",
    "n_orders: 0; n_new_orders: 0; n_disputes: 1; gmv_cents: 0."
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "med",
      "reasoning": "Three disputes among 29 orders warrant investigation, and ticket_drift is 1.4285542967774443. However, volume_z is only 0.31878835653166937, and the metrics do not establish thin buyer accounts, settlement extraction or failed delivery."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A campaign promoting higher-priced products could explain ticket drift. No campaign evidence is supplied, and volume_z provides little support for a pronounced sales ramp."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The reported rate is arithmetically consistent with 3 disputes divided by 29 orders, but record completeness, deduplication and denominator alignment remain unverified. Zero orders on the alert date can coexist with a dispute and does not itself establish a pipeline gap."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reserve",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Review the three dispute records for distinct transactions, reasons, status and underlying order dates; verify that the numerator and denominator follow the intended policy definition.",
    "Check shipment, delivery and customer-contact records for all three disputed orders and a small sample of recent orders. Repeated verified non-delivery would strengthen bust-out concerns; credible delivery evidence would weaken them.",
    "Reconcile refund requests, pending refunds and processed refunds with the reported zero refunds; identify unresolved cancellation or non-delivery complaints.",
    "Ask for dated campaign records and promoted product prices to test whether a documented marketing push explains ticket drift.",
    "Reconcile order, dispute and refund source records with the metric pipeline for missing or duplicated events. Corrected counts could dismiss the breach.",
    "Inspect buyer account history and linked-account concentration for recent orders; new_gmv_share alone does not establish thin or coordinated buyers."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "Merchant 53 breached AUP-06.1 on May 17: three disputes across 29 trailing-30-day orders, a 10.3% rate. The denominator is small, so individual records materially affect the result. Ticket drift is 1.4286, while volume_z is 0.3188; the metrics do not establish a sharp sales ramp. New-buyer GMV share is 14.3%. Zero recorded refunds do not establish successful fulfillment.\n\nRecommend a human-approved reserve holding a percentage of payouts while reviewing the three disputes, delivery evidence and unresolved refund requests. Select the percentage through the platform’s reserve process.\n\nBust-out remains a hypothesis. Verified repeated non-delivery, coordinated thin buyers and unresolved complaints would strengthen it and support considering a settlement pause. Credible delivery records, a documented campaign explaining ticket changes, or corrected dispute counts removing the breach would weaken or dismiss the alert. Reconcile source records before relying on the rate. Offboarding requires corroborated bust-out evidence, which is absent here."
}
